photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of named Cheyenne chiefs (Lean Bear, Standing in the Water, War Bonnet) in traditional quilled/beaded shirts, leggings, moccasins, and ornaments, documenting genuine Cheyenne dress and regalia.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Cheyenne man, High Toe, wearing a warrior shirt, quillwork leggings, moccasins, dentalium choker, ear ornaments, feather, and blanket, holding a pipe — a documentary photograph of Cheyenne dress and material culture.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of three Cheyenne men (White Antelope, High Toe, Little Chief) in traditional dress—decorated shirts, leggings, feathers, warbonnet, and ornaments—clearly documenting Cheyenne attire and appearance.

photo.name: photographic print; carte-de-visite
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); carte-de-visite
photo.reason: Studio carte-de-visite portrait of Lean Bear, a named Cheyenne chief, wearing a fringed warrior shirt, ear ornaments, blanket, embroidered leggings and moccasins — documentary photo of Cheyenne dress.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: A studio photograph of Little Robe, a named Cheyenne chief, in traditional dress including a quilled blanket, gorget, and moccasins, documenting Cheyenne dress and identity directly.

photo.name: photographic print; cabinet card
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); cabinet card
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Little Robe, identified Cheyenne chief, wearing a quillwork-decorated wool blanket, gorget, and moccasins alongside a military jacket; documentary photo of Cheyenne dress and a named individual clearly fits the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: The photo documents three Cheyenne men in traditional dress (dentalium necklace, hide blankets, leggings, moccasins) with a pack horse, matching the claimed ethnicity as a documentary portrait of their dress and daily life.

photo.name: stereoscope photograph
photo.title: stereoscope photograph (black and white)
photo.reason: Documentary portrait photograph of Little Wolf, a named Cheyenne chief, wrapped in a blanket and wearing embroidered moccasins, a genuine ethnographic/documentary photo of a Cheyenne individual.

photo.name: photographic print; glass negative
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); glass negative
photo.reason: Portrait photograph of Two Moons, a Northern Cheyenne chief, wearing a decorated headband and neck ornament — a documentary photo of a named Cheyenne individual in traditional dress, matching the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Cheyenne man in traditional dress—cloth shirt, wool blanket wrapped at waist, feathered headband, hair in braids—documenting Native American clothing and adornment, fitting the claimed ethnicity.

garment.name: Shirt
garment.title: Shirt
garment.reason: A fringed hide shirt with quillwork-decorated shoulder strips and a beaded/quilled bib front, consistent with Plains war shirts of the type made and worn by Cheyenne and neighboring Plains peoples; the Swedish museum notes even describe porcupine quillwork technique used on such garments.

household.name: säck, parfleche, sack, parflèche
household.title: säck, parfleche, sack, parflèche
household.reason: A painted rawhide parfleche (meat/food storage container) with typical geometric designs in red and green, explicitly noted by the museum's own expert (Douglas) as one of the finest examples, attributed to Cheyenne — a classic Plains parfleche form.

household.name: Parfleche
household.title: Parfleche
household.reason: A painted rawhide parfleche envelope with geometric designs, a classic Plains container type made and used by the Cheyenne for storing dried meat and belongings; fully consistent with the claimed ethnicity and category.

household.name: smoking-pipe-bag
household.title: smoking-pipe-bag
household.reason: A beaded hide pipe bag with long fringe, made and used by the Cheyenne (Plains peoples) for holding a pipe and tobacco; the geometric beadwork is classic Plains/Cheyenne style. Category is mislabeled "textile" but the object itself clearly belongs to this people.

household.name: Pipe bag
household.title: Pipe Bag
household.reason: A quilled/beaded hide pipe bag with fringe, geometric lane work and animal (deer/elk) figures, a classic Plains Cheyenne beadwork form; fits the claimed culture though category is better classified as a garment/bag accessory than "textile."

household.name: tobakspåse, tobaksväska
household.title: tobakspåse, tobaksväska
household.reason: A long fringed hide tobacco bag/pipe bag with quilled/beaded panels in geometric bands, a type characteristic of Plains peoples including the Cheyenne, and the museum attributes it to Cheyenne maker; the exhibition history (1878-79) supports an old, genuine Plains piece.

household.name: sadel
household.title: sadel
household.reason: The image shows a leather horse saddle with stirrups, wrapped rawhide pommel, and fringe decoration, attributed by the Field Museum provenance to the Northern Cheyenne — a plausible object made and used by Plains equestrian peoples.

household.name: säck, parfleche, sack, parflèche
household.title: säck, parfleche, sack, parflèche
household.reason: This is a painted rawhide parfleche storage bag with geometric designs typical of Plains peoples; the museum's own note specifically attributes this piece (no. 11) to the Cheyenne, distinguishing it from a related Blackfoot piece (no. 10), so there is direct evidence supporting the claimed attribution.

household.name: smoking-pipe-bag
household.title: smoking-pipe-bag
household.reason: The image shows a hide pipe bag with geometric beadwork and long fringe, a classic Plains item used by the Cheyenne for carrying a pipe and tobacco; it matches the claimed culture and use.

household.name: smoking-pipe-bag
household.title: smoking-pipe-bag
household.reason: This is a beaded skin pipe bag with geometric quillwork/beadwork panel and long fringe, a classic Plains/Cheyenne item, matching the museum's attribution to Cheyenne makers.

household.name: bag, bag, pipe bag
household.title: bag, bag, pipe bag
household.reason: A classic Plains-style beaded and quilled hide pipe bag with fringe, a form used by Cheyenne and other Plains peoples for carrying pipes and tobacco; consistent with Cheyenne material culture.

textile.name: bag
textile.title: bag
textile.reason: A beaded saddle bag with geometric quill/beadwork panels and long fringe, a classic Plains beadwork form attributed to Cheyenne makers; the object type and style fit the claimed culture.

painting-mss.name: Page
painting-mss.title: Maffet Ledger: Drawing
painting-mss.reason: A classic ledger-art drawing of a mounted warrior with a war bonnet and shield lancing a fallen enemy, made in graphite/watercolor/crayon on ledger paper — this is the well-documented Cheyenne (Maffet Ledger) narrative art tradition.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Maffet Ledger: Indian Shooting Gun
painting-mss.reason: A ledger drawing by a Cheyenne artist depicts a warrior firing a rifle beside his horse, a classic Plains ledger art scene documenting Cheyenne life and warfare.

painting-mss.name: Book
painting-mss.title: Maffet Ledger: Drawing
painting-mss.reason: A ledger-book drawing of a warrior on horseback in combat, done in graphite, watercolor and crayon — a classic Plains ledger art scene attributed to a Cheyenne artist (Maffet Ledger), depicting their own traditional pictorial narrative style.

painting-mss.name: oil painting
painting-mss.title: oil painting
painting-mss.reason: This is an oil portrait painted by a non-Native artist depicting a named Cheyenne chief in traditional dress (frill shirt, ornaments, pipe) — the subject is Cheyenne but the artwork itself is an outsider's depiction, a documentary-style ethnographic portrait rather than the culture pictured by outsiders in a derogatory or stylized colonial sense; it functions like a documentary portrait of dress and regalia, which is allowed.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Maffet Ledger: Battle at Adobe Walls
painting-mss.reason: A Plains ledger drawing depicting the Battle of Adobe Walls, showing a wagon and tipis under attack with arrow/hoofprint motifs, a classic Cheyenne narrative ledger art scene documenting a known historical event involving Southern Cheyenne warriors.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Maffet Ledger: Indian, Gun, and Horse
painting-mss.reason: This is a classic Plains ledger drawing from the Maffet Ledger, a documented Cheyenne (Southern/Northern) manuscript showing a warrior leading a horse with feathered regalia and a gun — a directly attributed Cheyenne pictorial artwork.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Maffet Ledger: Mounted Indian
painting-mss.reason: A ledger-art drawing of a mounted warrior with lance and bow, attributed to the Maffet Ledger (Southern/Northern Cheyenne), a classic traditional Plains pictorial art form made by Cheyenne artists.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Maffet Ledger: Wounded Mountain Lions
painting-mss.reason: This is a ledger drawing depicting two wounded mountain lions in graphite, watercolor, and crayon, a documented Cheyenne narrative art form of the reservation era; the Maffet Ledger is attributed to Southern/Northern Cheyenne artists.

instruments.name: rattle
instruments.title: rattle
instruments.reason: A gourd medicine rattle with hide handle, fur, and feather attachments and painted design, attributed by the museum to Cheyenne/Plains peoples — a plausible traditional Plains musical/ritual instrument.
